html:
Vanilla, a climbing orchid from Mexico, was brought to northeast Madagascar from nearby Réunion in the late 19th century, and the island now produces most of the world's natural vanilla.

The plant needs hand pollination outside Mexico, a method found by an enslaved boy on Réunion, Edmond Albius, in 1841. Growers in the Sava region around Antalaha and Sambava pollinate each flower by hand, then cure the pods for months.

Vanilla is one of the country's main exports, but prices swing wildly, and booms have brought theft, violence and sudden wealth to villages. Cyclones can wipe out a harvest. It ties Madagascar to the spread of American crops and to world food makers. The crop came by way of the sugar islands such as Mauritius and Réunion.
sum: Vanilla, a climbing orchid from Mexico, was brought to northeast Madagascar from nearby Réunion in the late 19th century, and the island now produces most of the world's natural vanilla.
